qa.question: Should I take JEE if I'm not sure between engineering and medicine?
qa.answer: If you cannot decide between engineering and medicine, take both NEET and JEE in parallel for the first three months of Class 11. Biology depth versus mathematical reasoning depth will reveal your real fit within twelve weeks. Most students cluster on one side organically; the few who don't typically choose engineering for broader career flexibility.

qa.question: Is NEET 2027 going to be computer-based?
qa.answer: NEET 2027 is expected to move toward computer-based test format based on NMC indications, though the official notification has not confirmed the year of full transition. Practice three or more CBT-mode mocks before exam day. CBT removes bubble-marking errors but introduces new navigation and screen-fatigue trade-offs that require deliberate adaptation.

qa.question: Is CBT mode harder than pen-paper for NEET?
qa.answer: CBT mode is harder for students used to pen-paper because there is no margin space for scratch calculations and navigation between questions costs three to five seconds extra each. CBT is easier on bubble-marking errors and answer-changes — net difficulty depends on CBT-mock practice. Practice three or more CBT mocks before NEET 2027.

qa.question: Why is parabola asked more in JEE Advanced than Main?
qa.answer: Parabola appears in four to six JEE Main questions per year versus six to ten in JEE Advanced because Advanced rewards multi-concept problems combining parabola with calculus, vectors, or coordinate-geometry tangents. JEE Main asks parabola-only direct-application; Advanced asks parabola-as-supporting-context. Mastering parabola for Advanced gives a real edge with limited extra time investment.

qa.question: How many electrostatics questions appear in JEE Main usually?
qa.answer: JEE Main Physics typically includes four to six electrostatics questions per shift — about sixteen to twenty-four marks out of one hundred. Capacitors, electric field calculations for symmetric distributions, and Gauss's law applications dominate. Electrostatics is the highest-weight Physics chapter alongside Mechanics; mastering it gains sixteen-plus marks consistently.
